title: Memory: lifecycle, garbage collection and the leaks you cause

videos.script:
JavaScript frees memory for you. {{gc}} You never write the line that gives an object's memory back. A part of the engine called the garbage collector finds objects nobody can reach any more and reclaims them.

That does not mean memory takes care of itself. {{leak}} A leak in JavaScript is not memory the collector forgot. It is memory your program is still holding on to, through a cache that only grows, a listener nobody removed, a timer nobody stopped. The collector is doing its job perfectly. The program is telling it everything is still in use.

{{measure}} Today you will watch memory rise and fall: a million objects allocated and released, a cache growing every hour, and the warning Node prints when listeners pile up.

{{fix}} Each leak has a small fix, and it is always the same idea: decide when something stops being needed, and let go of it then. {{weak}} And you will see where WeakRef fits, and why it is the tool of last resort rather than the first.
